root_cause.text: The parser did not check if the end of the header name reached the end of the string without finding a colon.

pattern: missing delimiter detection in parser
fix: Added a check in splitHeader to throw an IllegalArgumentException if nameEnd equals length.
guard: the check if (nameEnd == length) in splitHeader
lesson: Always verify that required delimiters are present before proceeding with parsing logic.

regression.given: An HttpRequestDecoder with a request containing a header 'Host:' followed by a newline and 'netty.io'
regression.when: the request string is written to the channel
regression.then: the decoder result should be a failure with an IllegalArgumentException

symptom.text: The server might accept HTTP/1.1 messages containing multiple Content-Length headers or both a Content-Length and a Transfer-Encoding: chunked header.

root_cause.text: The decoder did not explicitly check for or reject multiple Content-Length headers or the presence of both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in HTTP/1.1 messages.

pattern: accepting ambiguous HTTP headers
fix: In HttpObjectDecoder.readHeaders, added checks to throw IllegalArgumentException if multiple Content-Length headers are found or if both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding: chunked are present in HTTP/1.1 messages.
guard: the check in HttpObjectDecoder.readHeaders for contentLengthValuesCount > 1 and the check for contentLengthValuesCount > 0 combined with HttpUtil.isTransferEncodingChunked
lesson: Validate that HTTP/1.1 headers do not contain conflicting or duplicate fields that could lead to request smuggling.

regression.given: An HttpRequestDecoder is used to decode an HTTP/1.1 request with multiple Content-Length headers or both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding: chunked.
regression.when: The request is written to an EmbeddedChannel.
regression.then: The decoder result is a failure with an IllegalArgumentException.

symptom.text: Servers might treat a single HTTP request differently if they use different line delimiters, potentially allowing HTTP request smuggling or HTTP desync.
symptom.quote: if the frontend server does NOT do the same you can potentially allow a single HTTP request to be treated differently by the two servers

root_cause.text: The parser allowed bare LF or CR characters as line delimiters instead of enforcing CRLF.

pattern: inconsistent line delimiter handling
fix: Changed line delimiter searches from b'\n' to b'\r\n' in parse_header, get_header_lines, and ChunkedReceiver.received, and added checks for bare CR or LF in parse_header and get_header_lines.
guard: raise ParsingError("Bare CR or LF found in HTTP message") in parse_header
lesson: Enforce strict adherence to protocol-defined delimiters to prevent desynchronization attacks.

regression.given: a chunked encoding stream where the chunk end is not properly terminated with CRLF
regression.then: a BadRequest error is raised

symptom.text: The parser would continue processing a request even if the Content-Length header contained an invalid value or multiple values.

root_cause.text: A ValueError during integer conversion of the Content-Length header was caught and silently defaulted to 0.

pattern: silent failure on invalid input parsing
fix: The parse_header function was modified to raise a ParsingError instead of defaulting to zero when a ValueError occurs.
guard: raise ParsingError in parse_header
lesson: Fail fast when encountering malformed protocol headers instead of attempting to recover with default values.

regression.given: a request with content-length: abc or multiple content-length headers
regression.then: a ParsingError is raised with the message Content-Length is invalid

symptom.text: HTTP desync/HTTP request smuggling attacks could potentially provide multiple Transfer-Encoding headers that would not get appropriately treated by waitress.
symptom.quote: HTTP desync/HTTP request smuggling attacks could potentially provide multiple Transfer-Encoding headers that would not get appropriately treated by waitress

root_cause.text: The parser did not properly validate all encodings in a comma-separated list or handle multiple Transfer-Encoding values, potentially allowing unsupported encodings to pass.

pattern: improper validation of delimited list
fix: The parse_header function in HTTPRequestParser was updated to split the Transfer-Encoding header by commas, iterate through all encodings, and verify that any provided encoding is 'chunked'.
guard: The check in parse_header ensures all encodings in the list are checked against the supported set and raises TransferEncodingNotImplemented if an unsupported encoding is found.
lesson: Always validate every element in a delimited list of configuration or protocol parameters.

regression.given: A request with a Transfer-Encoding header containing an unsupported encoding like 'gzip'
regression.then: A TransferEncodingNotImplemented error is raised

symptom.text: Non-printable characters or specific non-RFC7230 whitespace characters were being accidentally removed from header values.

root_cause.text: Using the default strip() function which removes all whitespace characters, including non-printable ones like \x85.

pattern: overly aggressive string trimming
fix: The strip() method was updated to strip only space and tab characters in parse_header and the encoding list comprehension.
guard: value.strip(b" \t") and encoding.strip(" \t")
lesson: Only strip characters explicitly defined as whitespace by the relevant protocol specification.

regression.given: A request with Transfer-Encoding containing non-printable characters like \x85 or unicode sequences like \xe2\x84\xaa
regression.then: A TransferEncodingNotImplemented error is raised instead of the characters being silently stripped

rejected_quotes: We can not just call bare strip() here because it will also remove other non-printable characters

symptom.text: An object could be cloned with a modified prototype via the __proto__ key.

root_cause.text: The clone function processed the __proto__ key during iteration.

pattern: prototype pollution via object property injection
fix: The internals.clone function now skips the __proto__ key during the iteration of object keys.
guard: The check for key === '__proto__' in internals.clone.
lesson: Always sanitize or skip sensitive keys like __proto__ when cloning objects.

regression.given: an object containing a __proto__ property with a value
regression.when: Hoek.clone is called on that object
regression.then: the resulting cloned object should not have the property x from the __proto__ object

symptom.text: The __proto__ property could be used to pollute the prototype of objects.

root_cause.text: The deepCopy function did not check for the __proto__ key when iterating over source properties.

pattern: prototype pollution via unsafe property copying
fix: The deepCopy function was updated to skip the __proto__ property.
guard: The check 'name !== '__proto__'' in deepCopy.
lesson: Always sanitize or block sensitive keys like __proto__ during recursive object cloning.

regression.given: a payload containing a __proto__ property with a protoPollution value
regression.when: util.deepCopy is called with an empty object and the payload
regression.then: the resulting object should not have the protoPollution property on its prototype

symptom.text: Properties can be injected into the prototype of Object, Number, String, or Array via command line arguments.

root_cause.text: The parser allowed assignment to the __proto__ key and did not prevent traversing into built-in prototypes.

pattern: prototype pollution via object property assignment
fix: The setKey function was updated to explicitly return if a key is '__proto__' and to reset the target object to a new object or array if it matches a built-in prototype.
guard: The check 'if (key === '__proto__') return;' in setKey.
lesson: Prevent assignment to sensitive keys like __proto__ when parsing untrusted input.

regression.given: Arguments containing '__proto__' or paths leading to built-in prototypes like Array.prototype
regression.then: the built-in prototypes remain unpolluted

symptom.text: the prototype of objects could be polluted

root_cause.text: the key __proto__ was used directly when parsing dot notation

pattern: prototype pollution via unsafe key assignment
fix: the sanitizeKey function was introduced to replace __proto__ with ___proto___ during the parsing of keys
guard: sanitizeKey
lesson: sanitize keys that can modify object prototypes when performing deep assignments

regression.given: parser is called with arguments containing __proto__ in dot notation or as a standalone flag
regression.then: the resulting object contains ___proto___ instead of __proto__ and the global Object prototype remains unpolluted

symptom.text: An attacker could use a malicious tarball to write files outside the intended collection installation directory.

root_cause.text: The extraction process did not validate if the destination path of a tar entry remained within the target collection directory.

pattern: path traversal via archive extraction
fix: The function _extract_tar_file now uses os.path.abspath to resolve the destination path and checks if the resulting parent directory is within the target destination.
guard: The check in _extract_tar_file comparing b_parent_dir against b_dest.
lesson: Always validate that extracted file paths are contained within the intended destination directory.

regression.given: A tarball containing a file entry with a path component like '../../outside.sh'
regression.then: The installation should fail with an AnsibleError indicating the entry would be placed outside the collection directory

symptom.text: Files or directories could be extracted to locations outside the intended output directory, potentially overwriting sensitive system files.

root_cause.text: The extraction process did not validate that the resolved real paths of destination directories and files remained within the specified output path boundary.

pattern: directory traversal via path manipulation
fix: Introduced safeMakeDir and preventWritingThroughSymlink to validate that all resolved paths are descendants of the real output path and to prevent writing through symlinks in extractFile.
guard: safeMakeDir checks if realParentPath.indexOf(realOutputPath) !== 0
lesson: Always validate that resolved file paths remain within the intended destination boundary.

symptom.text: Authorization headers are passed to different domains during redirects.

root_cause.text: The client does not strip the authorization header when the redirect URL hostname differs from the original URL hostname.

pattern: sensitive credential leakage on cross-domain redirects
fix: In the HttpClient class, the code now iterates through headers and deletes any header named 'authorization' (case-insensitive) if the parsedRedirectUrl hostname does not match the parsedUrl hostname.
guard: check if parsedRedirectUrl.hostname !== parsedUrl.hostname and delete authorization header
lesson: Strip sensitive authentication credentials when following redirects to a different origin.

regression.given: a request with an authorization header is made to a URL that redirects to a different hostname
regression.then: the authorization header should be undefined in the resulting request headers

symptom.text: The client fails to recognize chunked transfer encoding when the encoding header contains multiple values.

root_cause.text: The code only checked if the entire transfer encoding string was equal to chunked.

pattern: improper parsing of comma-separated header values
fix: The setup_body function was updated to split the transfer encoding string by commas and check each part for the chunked value.
guard: the comma-splitting loop in setup_body
lesson: Always account for multiple values in comma-separated HTTP headers.

evidence.message_ignored: The message claims to better handle client input, but the code specifically addresses the parsing of the Transfer-Encoding header.

symptom.text: Properties like __proto__, constructor, or prototype could be overwritten or added to the global object or existing variables.

root_cause.text: The function allowed setting values on sensitive keys such as __proto__, constructor, or prototype.

pattern: prototype pollution via unsafe key assignment
fix: The zipObjectDeep function now checks if the key is '__proto__', 'constructor', or 'prototype' and returns the object early if a match is found.
guard: The check for '__proto__', 'constructor', or 'prototype' in zipObjectDeep.
lesson: Always validate or sanitize keys when performing deep object assignments to prevent prototype pollution.

regression.given: keys like '__proto__.a', 'constructor.b', or 'prototype.c' are passed to zipObjectDeep
regression.then: the global object and existing variables are not modified and no new properties are created

symptom.text: prototype pollution on unflatten

root_cause.text: the unflatten function allowed the use of the __proto__ key

pattern: prototype pollution via unsafe key assignment
fix: added a check in unflatten to return early if key1 is '__proto__'
guard: check for '__proto__' in unflatten
lesson: prevent assignment to sensitive object properties like __proto__

symptom.text: unknown

root_cause.text: The parser was tracking read bytes and checking against maxAbortedPayload even for non-aborted requests, and the resume logic was not properly checking for aborted requests in all states.

pattern: improper state management during request abortion
fix: Removed maxAbortedPayload tracking and logic in Parser and Client; updated _resume to check for aborted requests in both running and pending states; updated Request.onConnect to manage timeout timers correctly.
guard: check for request.aborted in _resume and Parser.onUpgrade
lesson: Always verify the validity of a request state before proceeding with operations like resuming or attaching sockets.

regression.given: a client request is aborted
regression.when: the parser processes data or the client resumes
regression.then: the aborted request should not trigger payload limits or continue processing

evidence.message_ignored: The message claims requestTimeout monitors from sent, but the code primarily removes maxAbortedPayload logic and refactors how requestTimeout is initialized and cleared.

symptom.text: An attacker could modify the prototype of objects by using specific JSON pointer keys.

root_cause.text: The set function allowed traversing and modifying sensitive keys like __proto__, prototype, or constructor.

pattern: unsafe property traversal via user input
fix: The api.set function was updated to skip tokens matching '__proto__', 'constructor', or 'prototype'.
guard: The check 'if (tok === "__proto__" || tok === "constructor" || tok === "prototype")' in api.set.
lesson: Always blacklist sensitive prototype-polluting keys when performing deep object updates.

regression.given: An object and a pointer targeting __proto__, prototype, or constructor properties
regression.then: The target object remains unpolluted

symptom.text: memory leak due to socket back pressure

root_cause.text: The parser was using socket.pause() and socket.resume() instead of controlling the underlying handle reading state.

pattern: improper flow control of underlying stream
fix: Replaced socket.pause() and socket.resume() with custom socketPause and socketResume functions that manipulate the handle reading state in Parser and connect.
guard: socketPause and socketResume functions in lib/core/client.js
lesson: Control the underlying stream reading state directly when implementing custom back pressure logic.

regression.given: a client request where the body is paused after receiving data
regression.when: the stream is resumed after a delay
regression.then: the internal readable state length remains below the high water mark

symptom.text: An attacker could overwrite arbitrary files on the system by using specially crafted archive filenames containing path traversal sequences.

root_cause.text: The unarchiving processes for Rar, Tar, and Zip did not validate that the extracted file destination remained within the intended target directory.

pattern: path traversal via archive filename
fix: Implemented the FilenameChecker interface with a CheckPath method in Rar, Tar, and Zip types to validate that the joined destination path starts with the target directory path.
guard: CheckPath in Rar, Tar, and Zip
lesson: Always validate that file paths extracted from untrusted archives are contained within the intended destination directory.

symptom.text: An attacker could modify the prototype of an object by setting magic properties.

root_cause.text: The set() function allowed setting properties named __proto__ or constructor.

pattern: prototype pollution via property injection
fix: The set() function now throws an error if the path targets __proto__ or constructor when includeInheritedProps is enabled.
guard: The check in set() for __proto__ and constructor properties.
lesson: Prevent modification of magic object properties to avoid prototype pollution.

symptom.text: modifying a locale with a key like __proto__ could pollute the object prototype

root_cause.text: the cache was initialized as a plain object literal

pattern: prototype pollution via object property injection
fix: changed the initialization of this.cache in the Y18N constructor to use Object.create(null)
guard: the use of Object.create(null) for the cache in the Y18N class
lesson: use null-prototype objects for internal caches to prevent prototype pollution

regression.given: a locale is set to '__proto__' and updateLocale is called with a property
regression.when: accessing the property on the prototype
regression.then: the property should be undefined

symptom.text: The parser could allow the modification of the prototype of objects, such as Object.prototype, through specially crafted section names or keys.

root_cause.text: The parser did not check if section names or keys were equal to '__proto__', allowing assignment to the prototype chain.

pattern: prototype pollution via unsafe keys
fix: The decode function was updated to skip processing if a section name or key is '__proto__', and the part traversal logic was updated to return early if a part matches '__proto__'.
guard: The check 'if (section === '__proto__')' in decode and 'if (part === '__proto__') return' in the parts traversal.
lesson: Always validate or sanitize keys used for object property assignment to prevent prototype pollution.

regression.given: An INI string containing sections or keys named '__proto__'
regression.then: The resulting object's prototype remains unchanged and does not contain the injected properties
